page: Microsoft Azure F2ams_v6 is a virtual machine configuration within the compute and memory-intensive Fams_v6 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provision stands at 16.0 GB total, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 instructions including VNNI and BF16, as well as AES and SHA cryptographic extensions. The server does not bundle local ephemeral storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for persistent and temporary files.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong single-core CPU throughput, logging a score of 3080.08 on stress-ng and 2066.0 on Geekbench single-core evaluations. Text processing performance is also notably strong at 2468.0 points. Because the instance possesses only two physical execution threads, multi-threaded throughput scales proportionally lower, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 3838.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng result of 6118.06. Memory benchmarks reflect 38.9 GB/sec on large-block uncached reads and 28.08 GB/sec on writes, positioning memory bandwidth in the average to lower distribution relative to larger instances. Small language model inference reaches 556.46 prompt tokens per second and 152.1 generation tokens per second for a 135M parameter model.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio yields a high memory allocation relative to compute capacity, making the instance cost-efficient for memory-sensitive tasks that do not demand extensive parallel core execution. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on attached managed disks, which introduces external I/O considerations. Microsoft Azure F2ams_v6 is best matched to lightweight databases, text processing pipelines, backend microservices, caching layers, and development runtimes prioritizing high single-thread clock speed and dedicated memory over high multi-threaded concurrency.
description: Microsoft Azure F2ams_v6 is a dedicated virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 2 vCPUs and 2 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it features an x86_64 architecture paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an expansive 8.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU supports AVX-512 vector execution, VNNI, BF16, and cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU resources, depending entirely on remote storage volumes. Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-core performance alongside average multi-core and uncached memory bandwidth due to the compact two-core footprint. This allocation provides high memory density per compute thread, making it technically well-suited for lightweight database engines, memory-resident caching, string and text processing routines, and single-threaded service endpoints that benefit from 3.7 GHz clock rates and ample memory space.
